problem:
The population of students $P(t)$ in a school can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.016(2\,500-P),
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, measured in years. If the initial population of the school is $800$ students, calculate the population after $4$ years. Round your answer to the nearest integer.

examples.problem: In an aquarium, there are initially $20$ fish. After $30$ weeks, the number of fish is $50.$ Assuming inhibited growth, calculate the number of fish after $100$ weeks if the maximum capacity of the aquarium is $90$ fish.
examples.worked_solution:
The rate at which the number of fish $N(t)$ changes is proportional to the difference between the total number of fish and the current number of fish. Therefore, we have the inhibited growth equation

$$
\dfrac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}t}=k\left(a-N\right),
$$

where $a$ is the maximum capacity of the aquarium, and $k > 0$ is a constant of proportionality.

In our case, $a = 90$ fish, and we have

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d} N}{\mathrm{d} t} = k(90-N).
$$

First, we integrate our differential equation by separating the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dN}{90-N} & =k\,dt \\ \int \frac{dN}{90-N} & =\int k\,dt \\ -\operatorname{ln}⁡|90-N| & =kt+C\end{aligned}
$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited growth equation, we have $90 - N > 0$ for all $t \ge 0.$
Next, we solve for $N(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}90-N & ={e}^{-kt-C} \\ 90-N & ={e}^{-C}{e}^{-kt} \\ 90-N & =K{e}^{-kt} \\ N & =90-K{e}^{-kt}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $K=e^{-C}$ is a constant of integration. 

We're told that the initial number of fish was $20.$ So, we apply the initial condition $N(0)=20,$ and solve for $K{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =20 \\ 90-K{e}^{0} & =20 \\ 90-K & =20 \\ K & =70\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following expression for $N(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
N(t)=90 - 70 e^{-kt}
$$

We're also told that, after $30$ weeks, the number of fish is $50.$ So, applying the condition $N(30)=50,$ we can solve for $k{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(30) & =50 \\ 90-70{e}^{-30k} & =50 \\ 40 & =70{e}^{-30k} \\ {e}^{-30k} & =\frac{4}{7} \\ -30k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{7}) \\ k & =-\frac{1}{30}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{7})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is

$$
N(t)=90-70e^{(t/30)\,\ln\left(4/7\right)}.
$$

Finally,  the number of fish after $t=100$ weeks is

$$
\begin{aligned}N(100) & =90-70{e}^{(100/30)\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(4/7)} \\  & =79.161… \\  & ≈79\,\text{fish},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

feedback.problem: A data center initially contains $320$ computers. The number of computers in the data center $C(t)$ increases at a rate that obeys an inhibited growth model, where $t\ge 0$ is the time in months. If the maximum capacity of the data center is $1000$ computers, which differential equation could be used to model the number of computers? Assume that $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the number of computers in the data center obeys an inhibited growth model, the rate at which the number of computers changes is proportional to the difference between the maximum capacity and the number of computers in the data center. Therefore, we have the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}=k(a-C),
$$

where $a$ is the maximum capacity of the data center, and $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

In our case, $a=1000$ computers, and we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}=k(1000-C).
$$
